title: Claude Haiku 5.5: Anthropic's cheapest, fastest small model
summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.

title: OpenAI announces GPT-6 and "Intelligent UI for everyone"
summary: OpenAI published an announcement titled "GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone", introducing the next generation of the model family behind ChatGPT.

title: Chrome is shipping support for JPEG XL images
summary: Google's Chrome team says the browser is shipping support for JPEG XL, a modern image format designed to keep photos sharp at smaller file sizes.

title: SynthID Detector goes public
summary: SynthID Detector, a tool for checking content for SynthID — Google's invisible watermark on AI-generated media — now has its own public site.

title: Margaret Hamilton, computing pioneer, has died
summary: MIT reports the death of Margaret Hamilton, the computing pioneer known for leading the software work behind NASA's Apollo missions.

title: Liquid AI releases open d1 decision models for devices
summary: Liquid AI released two open "decision models" — small models built to pick the right action rather than write long answers: d1-3B and an experimental d1-omni-600M that also handles more than text.

title: NVIDIA fine-tunes Nemotron to gold-level olympiad results
summary: NVIDIA describes how it fine-tuned one open model family, Nemotron, to reach gold-level results at both the International Olympiad in Informatics (programming) and the International Mathematical Olympiad.

title: The AI model you need doesn't exist? Have an assistant build it
summary: Hugging Face published a walkthrough of ML Intern, an AI assistant that trains small custom models from a plain-language prompt.

title: Falcon ASR: speech recognition built with Arabic in mind
summary: The Technology Innovation Institute released Falcon ASR, a model that turns spoken audio into text, with a focus on Arabic — including Emirati speech — as well as English and other languages.

title: Whistle: speech-to-text in a 16.9 MB package
summary: Cactus Compute introduced Whistle, a speech-to-text model that takes up just 16.

title: Prison sentence for faking music streams with bots
summary: A US man has been sentenced to prison for using bot farms to generate fake streams of music, The Quietus reports.

title: GitHub: protecting passwords and keys has to keep up with AI
summary: GitHub argues that developers aren't getting more careless about leaking passwords and access keys — they're being outpaced by how much software AI now helps them produce.

title: GitHub rebuilds its Git backbone for AI agents
summary: GitHub is rebuilding the Git infrastructure that stores and serves every repository — while the site keeps running.

title: StepFun's Step 5 Preview appears with a 1M-token memory
summary: Step 5 Preview, a new model from Chinese AI company StepFun, has shown up on OpenRouter, a service that gives developers access to many AI models through one account.

title: An Anthropic AI model sent police a false tip on an unsolved murder
summary: NBC Philadelphia reports that, according to police, an Anthropic AI model submitted a tip about an unsolved Philadelphia murder — and the tip was false.

title: Microsoft joins the small "decision model" trend
summary: Microsoft introduced Microsoft-Decision-1, a model built for fast decision-making rather than long written answers.

title: AI digs through 400 years of archives and finds forgotten things
summary: A writer pointed AI at four centuries of archival records and surfaced a forgotten meteorite, lost rhinos and more.

title: Terry Tao on trusting AI in mathematics
summary: Terence Tao, one of the world's best-known mathematicians, wrote about Lean — software that checks mathematical proofs step by step — and what it means for reliability as AI starts producing proofs.

title: Developers want software that wastes less computing power
summary: GitHub and the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication surveyed over 1,000 GitHub users and found strong demand for tools and guidance to cut wasted compute.

title: How Ai2 decides who gets the GPUs
summary: The Allen Institute for AI described the scheduler it built for its GPU clusters — the shared pools of chips used to train AI models.

title: Hugging Face Transformers can now run llama.cpp models
summary: Hugging Face's Transformers library, the most widely used toolkit for running open AI models in Python, now runs llama.

title: Anthropic expands its program for vetted security professionals
summary: Anthropic launched an expanded Cyber Verification Program, which gives qualifying security professionals access to Claude's advanced cyber capabilities with fewer automatic blocks.

title: AI models struggled to match a human algorithmic breakthrough
summary: Research group Epoch AI tested whether recent AI models could reproduce a genuine human innovation in algorithm design, and found they struggled to match it.

title: Rampart hides personal details right inside your browser
summary: Rampart is a new tool that removes personal information, such as names and contact details, from text directly on your device, without sending it anywhere.

title: Microsoft releases containers to keep AI agents in bounds
summary: Microsoft released version 1.

title: AI agents took apart a classic shooter game
summary: A developer let AI agents reverse-engineer a first-person shooter, turning the finished game back into readable code, and used about 500 billion tokens (units of text AI processes) to do it.

title: Teaching language models to read raw bytes
summary: A paper in Nature describes retrofitting existing language models so they work directly on bytes — the raw building blocks of digital text — instead of on tokens, the word chunks most models split text into.

title: Google's Finnish data centre work halted over forest clearing
summary: The Guardian reports that work linked to Google's data centres in Finland has been temporarily halted, with critics saying forest was cut without the required environmental impact assessment.

title: New York City's "Click to Cancel" rule is now in effect
summary: New York City's rule requiring businesses to make cancelling a subscription as easy as signing up has taken effect.

title: Fingerprints are the new cookies
summary: A widely shared essay argues that browser fingerprinting — identifying you from the unique mix of your device and browser settings — is replacing cookies as the main way websites track you.

title: Karpathy: people increasingly disagree about what AI can do
summary: Andrej Karpathy, a well-known AI researcher and OpenAI co-founder, posted that the gap in shared understanding of what AI language models can actually do is widening.

title: GitHub: three skills that matter more as AI writes code
summary: GitHub says AI is reshaping developer careers and names three skills to strengthen: directing AI agents, critically reviewing their output, and keeping human judgment at the centre.

title: A public leaderboard for AI voices in many languages
summary: Hugging Face launched the Open TTS Leaderboard, which scores text-to-speech models (AI that reads text aloud) across multiple languages and on voice cloning — copying a specific person's voice.

title: Sakana AI: AI systems that improve themselves as a group
summary: Tokyo-based Sakana AI published research on recursive self-improvement through collective intelligence — many AI agents working together to make the overall system better over time, rather than one model improving alone.

title: Hackers defrost supermarket fridges across Europe
summary: Tom's Hardware reports a cyberattack that hit supermarket refrigeration across Europe: attackers remotely triggered the fridges' automatic defrosting.

title: GLM-Legal: an AI model aimed at legal work
summary: Chinese AI company Z.

title: Anthropic tightens defenses against model copying
summary: Anthropic published research on strengthening its defenses against "distillation attacks" — when someone trains their own AI model on another model's answers to copy its abilities cheaply.

title: OpenAI's Codex tool runs a background program by default
summary: A widely discussed bug report says OpenAI's Codex CLI, a coding assistant that runs on your computer, installs a self-updating background program by default.

title: Paper: AI models can provably hide abilities
summary: A new research paper argues that AI models can be built to hide arbitrary capabilities in a way that can be mathematically proven.

title: Teaching GitHub Copilot about your codebase
summary: GitHub published a beginner's guide to the Copilot app that shows how to add custom instructions and skills to a repository, set up custom agents, and connect MCP servers — plug-ins that give the assistant extra tools, such as Playwright for controlling a web browser.

title: Intel's D270: an AI accelerator with up to 480 GB of memory
summary: Intel lists the D270, a data-centre GPU built as an AI accelerator, with up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X memory — a type of memory more common in laptops and phones than in AI chips.

title: Google DeepMind lists Gemini 4 Argon
summary: Google DeepMind's Gemini models page now features Gemini 4 Argon, a new model in the family that powers Google's Gemini assistant.

title: Ledger confirms a spy chip was behind crypto wallet thefts
summary: Ledger, which makes hardware devices for storing cryptocurrency, confirmed that a spy implant hidden in wallets was behind thefts from its customers, BleepingComputer reports.

title: Character.ai files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
summary: Character.

title: A capable AI assistant that runs privately on your own device
summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.

title: Physical Intelligence opens its robot AI to other companies
summary: Robotics AI company Physical Intelligence launched a beta of its API, offering its most advanced models to anyone building robots.

title: GitHub's AI finds leaked passwords with fewer false alarms
summary: GitHub built a context-aware classifier — a model that looks at the code around a suspected password or access key, not just the string itself — for its secret scanning.

title: ReviewBench: an open test for AI code reviewers
summary: GitHub launched ReviewBench, a benchmark for AI agents that review code.

title: AI simulates extreme weather at 3 km detail for a fraction of the cost
summary: The Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) released HiRO-ACEv2, an AI climate emulator — a model that imitates expensive physics-based climate simulations.

title: Experts: AI "hacking" incidents come down to basic security lapses
summary: Security experts quoted by CSO Online argue that recent reports of AI agents hacking systems aren't about AI going rogue — they're about AI labs skipping basic containment and monitoring.

title: Google is quietly linking your phone number across accounts
summary: Android Authority reports that Google is automatically linking your phone number to every Google account signed in on your phone, without asking.

title: OpenCode 2.0 is out
summary: OpenCode, an open-source AI coding assistant, has released version 2.

title: Security researcher: passkeys are not a trap
summary: Security researcher Scott Helme pushes back on the worry that passkeys — sign-ins that use your phone or laptop's fingerprint, face or PIN instead of a password — lock you into one company's ecosystem.

title: GitHub rebuilds star history with 99% fewer requests
summary: GitHub launched a new API for a repository's star history — how a project's popularity has grown over time.
